steps.name: Salmon import to gene-level counts
steps.context: Files: /eval-four-models-v2-without-salmon-quant-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/quant/<sample>/quant.sf (30,147 rows, columns Name, Length, ...), /eval-four-models-v2-without-salmon-quant-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/quant/tx2gene.csv (transcript, gene), /eval-four-models-v2-without-salmon-quant-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition). The quant.sf directories sit in the same parent as tx2gene.csv, so list the directories and exclude tx2gene.csv when enumerating samples.
steps.question: Can the per-sample Salmon quant.sf files be aggregated into a consistent gene-level count matrix for all 12 samples (6 treated, 6 control) using the provided tx2gene.csv, and what fraction of transcripts/reads map?
steps.description: Aggregate the 12 per-sample Salmon quant.sf files (30,147 transcripts) to gene-level counts using tx2gene.csv and write the gene-level count matrix, TPM matrix, and QC summary.
acceptance_criteria: A gene-level count matrix and a gene-level abundance/TPM matrix exist on disk, one row per gene, one column per sample, with all 12 sample columns matching the sample identifiers in metadata.csv
The import log reports, per sample, how many transcripts were read, how many mapped through tx2gene.csv, and how many were dropped as unmapped
Genes absent from tx2gene.csv or duplicated in the map are quantified and handled explicitly (aggregated or dropped with a written note), never silently
The design is confirmed as 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, with no covariates beyond condition, matching the delivered metadata table

steps.name: Differential expression treated vs control
steps.context: Input is the gene-level count matrix from T1S1. Design is ~condition with exactly two levels (treated, control) and no batch or paired structure. Environment has no network, so no external annotation downloads; org.Hs.eg.db 3.23.0 is installed for symbol mapping.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control skin samples (6 vs 6), at what effect sizes and FDR, and is the design free of technical outliers?
steps.description: Fit DESeq2 on the gene-level counts (design ~ condition), test treated vs control by Wald test, apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction and apeglm LFC shrinkage, and export the ranked results table plus diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A results table exists with, per gene: Ensembl gene ID, baseMean, log2FC (shrunk), lfcSE, Wald statistic, raw p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, and the gene symbol joined from org.Hs.eg.db where available
The table is sorted and saved both as a full table and as a filtered significant set (padj < 0.05), with the filtered set's size reported
Diagnostic outputs exist: MA plot, volcano plot, sample-to-sample distance heatmap/PCA colored by condition, and the dispersion-fit summary
The number of genes retained after filtering, the number of genes tested, the number of hits at padj<0.05, and the up/down split at FDR<0.05 are reported numerically
Any sample flagged as an outlier by Cook's distance is reported rather than silently removed

steps.name: WikiPathways enrichment of DE genes
steps.context: Input is the shrunk-LFC-ranked gene table from T1S2 (Ensembl IDs plus symbols). Reference data: the human WikiPathways GMT under /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human (HGNC gene symbols, '%'-delimited descriptor on the first field). Symbol mapping via org.Hs.eg.db (ENTREZID/SYMBOL/ENSEMBL keys are all carried by org.Hs.eg.db). Environment has no network access, so no MSigDB download; the provisioned WikiPathways human GMT is the pathway resource.
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes up- or down-regulated in treated versus control skin, and which leading-edge genes drive them?
steps.description: Map DE genes from Ensembl IDs to HGNC symbols using org.Hs.eg.db, then run fgsea on the signed shrunk-log2FC-ranked gene list against the human WikiPathways GMT.
acceptance_criteria: A fgsea results table exists with pathway name, size, NES, p-value, and FDR for all tested WikiPathways human pathways, sorted by FDR
Only pathways with at least 10 and at most 500 genes after ID mapping are tested, and the count of tested pathways is reported
Leading-edge genes are extracted for the top pathways and reported alongside the DE results
If the WikiPathways human GMT or org.Hs.eg.db mapping is unavailable at run time, the step writes a clear failure note instead of substituting another species' resource

The report distinguishes established atopic-dermatitis-relevant signals (e.g. IL-4/IL-13 axis, keratinocyte differentiation) from pathways that pass FDR but lack a literature link, without overclaiming mechanism

plan.title: AD skin Salmon-to-DESeq2 differential expression
plan.analytical_narrative: The inputs are 12 per-sample Salmon directories (quant.sf, 30,147 transcripts each) plus tx2gene.csv and a 12-row metadata table (condition: treated vs control, unpaired, single batch). No gene-level count matrix exists, so the first step must aggregate transcript-level Salmon estimates to gene level with tximport (countsFromAbundance="lengthScaledTPM"), which corrects for transcript length changes across conditions and produces counts usable by DESeq2 despite the non-integer NumReads. The second step runs the differential expression model itself: DESeq2 Wald test on ~condition, Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and apeglm log2FC shrinkage to produce a stable ranked gene table for treated-vs-control. The third step interprets the ranked list biologically: genes are mapped from Ensembl IDs to HGNC symbols with org.Hs.eg.db, and the signed-shrunk-LFC ranking is tested against the human WikiPathways GMT with fgsea, since the environment has no network access and no other pathway resource for Homo sapiens is provisioned. With n=6 per arm the study is powered only for large effects, so the plan reports effect sizes and confidence honestly rather than relying on thresholds alone.
